newsitem.title: UK: Go-Ahead up on hopes of better results.
newsitem.headline: Go-Ahead up on hopes of better results.

text.p: Shares in Go-Ahead Plc advanced on Wednesday amid speculation the British rail and bus operator would, like rival FirstBus, report a good result for the year ending on June 30, analysts said.
By 0845 GMT the stock was up 21-1/2p to 447-1/2p.
"I guess this is the expectation that Go-Ahead will also deliver pretty good figures", an analyst said.
FirstBus Plc reported on Tuesday that its pre-tax profit surged to 51 million stg from 22 million stg as the operating margin rose to 15.2 percent from 13.6 percent.

The fact that FirstBus managed to achieve an operating margin of 16.6 percent in the north of England would fuel hopes that Go-Ahead, which is focused on the north, could do even better, the analyst said.
Earlier this year, Go-ahead dismissed a report that it and four other transport companies faced heavy losses on their rail franchises.
Go-Ahead, which is due to report its annual results in September, posted a pre-tax profit of 11.87 million stg in financial year 1996 on sales of 134.8 million stg.
Go-Ahead shares slipped from their year high of 535p set in mid-March to a low of 418p marked on June 6.
